head: 87757fc
target: Session start repairs a clone whose local core.hooksPath names a directory the repo no longer tracks, and no code path writes hooks while any effective core.hooksPath is in effect.

questions.prompt: Before this fix, a clone pulled the commit that removed the repo's once-tracked .githooks directory, and its local core.hooksPath still named .githooks. Every push from it sailed through ungated, and nothing anywhere reported a problem. Walk through why that state was silent.

options.label: Git falls back to .git/hooks when core.hooksPath names a missing directory, but the hook there lacked the executable bit, so git skipped it without an error.

Git executes hooks from the directory core.hooksPath names; when that directory is missing it silently runs no hooks at all — no error, no fallback — and the old install path never read the config, so a hook that was written and a hook that runs were indistinguishable.
Push fails outright while core.hooksPath names a missing directory, but session start's || true swallowed the failure, so nobody saw it.
The removal commit deleted the gate's pre-push hook along with the directory, and session start installs only into fresh clones.

key_points: git resolves hook execution through core.hooksPath, and when it names a missing directory git silently runs no hooks — no error and no fallback to .git/hooks
the old install path never read core.hooksPath, so it could not tell a hook that runs from one that sits inert

questions.prompt: The selftest additions give the suite its first scenarios where git's hook execution is redirected by core.hooksPath. What blind spot does that close?

options.label: Nothing verified that install leaves a foreign pre-push hook in .git/hooks alone.

Every earlier scenario assumed git runs hooks from .git/hooks, so a clone whose config redirected hooks elsewhere could keep a hook file that exists yet never executes, and no check could tell the two apart.
Nothing verified that session start installs the hook in a fresh clone of an opted-in repo.
Nothing verified that the shell guard denies a git -c core.hooksPath=... push.

key_points: before the fix the suite never exercised a hooksPath redirect during installation, so 'the hook file exists' and 'the hook runs' were never distinguished
the new checks pin behavior through real session start and real git config: the stale config is unset with a notice, the manager's directory stays empty, and install refuses

questions.prompt: Counterfactual: write_hook drops the refusal and installs anyway whenever an effective core.hooksPath exists — into .git/hooks, or into the directory the config names. Which failures does the refusal as written prevent? Pick all that hold.

options.label: A push erroring out because two pre-push hooks run in conflict.
A hook written into .git/hooks that silently never runs, because git executes hooks from the configured directory — the gate sits inert while pushes pass.
Overwriting a hook manager's own generated pre-push in a directory the plugin does not own.
A later manager reinstall regenerating its pre-push and silently deleting the gate.

key_points: writing into .git/hooks under an effective hooksPath is a silent no-op: the file exists but never executes
writing into the configured directory clobbers the manager's hook, and a manager reinstall can regenerate it and silently delete the gate
refusing with the one line to add keeps the manager sole owner of its directory while still telling the agent how to get a gate

questions.prompt: New case: a teammate's clone carries a GLOBAL core.hooksPath pointing at a directory they deleted last week. They start a session in this opted-in repo. By design, what happens, what must they do to get a gate, and why is this treated differently from the stale local hooksPath that session start repairs?
key_points: sync leaves the global config alone: the repair unsets only a local hooksPath, because global config is the user's deliberate machine-wide setup — not damage this repo's history caused — and an unattended session-start hook must not rewrite config that affects other repos
write_hook still refuses, since git reads the merged config: with any effective hooksPath an install into .git/hooks would sit inert, so no gate is written while the config stands
the refusal text still reaches the agent — it goes to stderr, which sync's stdout discard does not touch — and session start exits 0: the clone is ungated but nobody is left uninformed
a gate returns only when the user repairs their own config or adds 'quizgate check || exit 1' to the hook their manager runs
